newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher optimistic for Piakau-1 well.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher optimistic for Piakau-1 well.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy is optimistic oil flows from its Piakau-1 well in Taranaki will prove to be commercial, but further testing is still required, the company said on Thursday.
During a five-hour production test on Wednesday, the central Taranaki well's flow rate was about 1,400 barrels with a gas to oil ratio of about 1000 standard cubic feet of gas to each barrel.

Company spokesman Barry Akers told the New Zealand Press Association it was too early to predict what the well's potential reserves may be. The fractured nature of the Tikorangi limestone formation the well targeted also meant flow rates could change.
"We would want to see how it flows for a little while longer before we made any definitive statements about it," he told NZPA.
The side-tracked well was sunk to re-test the potential of the Tikorangi limestone in the Piakau segment of the Ahuroa-Piakau prospect.
Fletcher Challenge also said it was currently casing the Kaimiro-15 well for completion.
Akers said the results from the well, spudded two weeks ago, were "quite good" with the company again cautiously optimistic.
The well had also provided promising data on its secondary exploration target, the Moki Sands of Upper Manganui formation.
